title: Twinbridge pilot outreach notebook
content:
Quick notes to self on Twinbridge (small-mid fin services platform) — working draft, do not share externally yet.

Account at-a-glance:
- HQ: Chicago. Series B (2022). ~300 employees, heavy on backend payments infra.
- Tech stack: Go microservices, Kafka, Postgres, some TF serving for models. Mostly AWS.
- Known pain: rising costs on 3rd-party LLM API usage (chat/assistants), high variance in latency for customer-facing agents.
- Primary sponsor: Alex Moreno (Dir, Platform Eng) — intro via Cassie (established contact, previously at Meridian).

Why Redwood might fit:
- Need: predictable per-call latency and lower unit cost for high-concurrency chat + embeddings for search.
- Win themes: Dedicated reserved pools for consistent p95, prefix caching for repeated customer prompts, private deployment option for regulated verticals.
- Quick value props to highlight: 30-50% TCO reduction on token spend for steady workloads (via caching + batching), consistent 99th pctl latency SLA, and rollout control for model updates.

Account research snippets (sources + assumptions):
- Job postings: multiple SRE + infra hiring in past 6 months -> scaling constraints.
- Engineering blog (May 2025): moving more features into real-time assistants, called out "cost spikes from API usage".
- Legal: standard SOC2, exploring FedRAMP-lite for a gov pilot (longer sales horizon).

Outbound hypothesis and experiment plan:
- Hypothesis: If we offer a 6-week technical pilot (Dedicated capacity, simple chat + embeddings integration, performance + cost report), Twinbridge will convert to a 6–12 month reserved capacity commit.
- Success metrics: reduce per-response cost by >=30% (baseline = current provider invoices), p95 latency <= 300ms for typical query mix, 1 internal team using the assistant in prod.
- Duration: 6 weeks. Commitment asked: 2 devs + 4 hours/week of infra time; access to a staging dataset (anonymized) and a small support/trial budget ($5k credits).

Suggested outbound cadence (sequence w/ personalization hooks):
- Email 1 (intro) — short, value-led, reference Alex + Cassie: subject: "Pilot idea: predictable assistant latency + cost control for Twinbridge". Body bullets: quick problem statement, what we would deliver in 6 weeks, ask for 20–30m tech sync.
- Email 2 (data ask) — 4 days later: share an anonymized sample cost model (one-pager) and ask for a small dataset extract for a scoped test.
- Call / VM script: quick 10–15 min discovery -> 3 questions: (1) current monthly LLM spend and burst patterns, (2) most critical latency P95/SLOs, (3) data restrictions/regulatory constraints.
- Email 3 (offer) — 7 days after call: tailored pilot proposal + timeline + success metrics + named engineers on Redwood side.

Outbound draft snippets (use these directly in outreach)
- Short intro email:
  Hi Alex — Cassie suggested I reach out. At Redwood we help infra-heavy platforms get predictable cost and latency for user-facing assistants without rebuilding inference stacks. For Twinbridge a quick 6-week pilot could: (a) show a 30%+ reduction in token cost by applying caching and batching, (b) give a p95 latency map across customer journeys, and (c) leave you with a deployable config that your platform team can operate. Are you open to a short tech sync next week?

- Follow-up email if no reply:
  Re-sending in case this slipped through — we’ve run the same pilot with two other fintechs and captured real token-level savings. If 20–30m is doable I can walk through the exact playbook.

Call script bullets (for SDR or AE):
- 30s intro: purpose + Cassie intro.
- Diagnostic questions: what does a typical user query look like? Are you doing embeddings for search/rerank? What percent of requests are realtime vs batch?
- Pain check: have you seen cost surprises or tail latency impacting conversion?
- Quick pitch: we can run a short Scoped Pilot (dev effort estimate, infra changes, expected results).
- Next step ask: schedule 60m runbook review with Alex + infra lead + Redwood engineer.

Objection handling (quick notes)
- "We already have a contract / are locked in": ask for usage vs contract; propose hybrid runway where we handle overflow/downgrade bursts or do shadow testing on select traffic.
- "Security/reg compliance concerns": highlight Private deployment and KMS/HSM integrations + audit logs; offer an architecture walkthrough with SRE + security.
- "No headcount to support pilot": propose a lower-touch pilot where Redwood engineers take on the majority of integration work for first 2 weeks (paid trial credits).
- "Won't see cost savings": offer to model their current invoices and run a matched benchmark on a sample workload before any contract.

Pricing thought starters (internal only)
- Pilot pricing: $5k credits + discounted pilot rate for dedicated capacity ($/GPU-hour) for 6 weeks.
- Upsell after pilot: 3-tier reserved capacity (small/med/large) with add-on observability retention and support.

Runbook for pilot (engineering touchpoints)
- Week 0: kickoff + data access; establish staging environment and provide integration SDK + quickstart.
- Week 1: baselining (current provider metrics) + synthetic load to match percentiles.
- Week 2–4: apply caching/batching profiles; iterate model variants and measure cost/latency.
- Week 5: final report + readiness review; provide rollout plan + rollback safety checks.
- Week 6: handover + optional recommendation for Dedicated sizing + SLOs.

Open questions / unknowns (need to validate on first call):
- Concrete monthly LLM spend and invoice structure (per-token vs per-request).
- Whether Twinbridge will allow us to run shadow traffic in staging or production.
- Any PII/data residency restrictions for user messages.
- Who is the legal point of contact for trial T&Cs.

Next immediate steps (today):
- Personal: craft the short intro email and put in Outreach sequence by EOD.
- Ops: ask Cassie for a warm intro to Alex (short intro blurb + context).
- Engineering: ping Elliot to draft pilot quickstart and estimate minimal infra time (1–2 pages).

Misc notes / phrases to A/B test in emails:
- "predictable p95 latency" vs "99th percentile latency"
- "token cost reduction" vs "monthly LLM spend reduction"
- include a one-line case study or a link to a short benchmark PDF if they ask for proof.

Scratch ideas (longer term):
- If pilot successful, propose a developer self-serve playbook for Twinbridge: pre-baked SDKs, sample configs, and a shared dashboard for business stakeholders to monitor cost.
- Explore channel partnership if Twinbridge resells to regional banking customers (co-sell motion).

---
Notes to self (todo list):
- [ ] Write the intro email and save templates in Outreach sequences.
- [ ] Get Cassie intro (ask for 1–2 line note).
- [ ] Draft pilot SOW template (legal) and send to Noah for review.
- [ ] Schedule internal sync with Elliot + Noah this week.

End of notebook entry.
